newsitem.title: CHINA: China foreign office in HK names spokesman - paper.
newsitem.headline: China foreign office in HK names spokesman - paper.

text.p: China's Foreign Ministry office in Hong Kong has named a spokesman to explain how the central government will handle the new Special Region's foreign relations, a Hong Kong newspaper said.

The independent Chinese-language Sing Tao newspaper said Gong Jianzhong would be spokesman for Beijing's mission, inaugurated on Tuesday when China took over Hong Kong from the British. His background was not identified.
China earlier signalled it was downgrading the role of its Xinhua News Agency branch, Beijing's official Hong Kong mission and watchdog during British colonial rule.
Zhang Junsheng, deputy director of Xinhua here, said on Thursday he ceased to be Beijing's spokesman.
The Xinhua mission in some ways acted as a shadow government and critic of the colonial administration, with Xinhua deputy directors tracking specific policy areas.
The Hong Kong Economic Times said on Saturday Xinhua chief Zhou Nan would step down after seven years in office.
Jiang Enzhou, formerly China's ambassador to London, would succeed Zhou in August, the newspaper said, adding that there would be a restructuring of Xinhua's departments soon.
